title: Connectors: how Power Platform apps, flows and agents reach other services
summary: The connector definitions, licensing statements and governance controls are supported by Microsoft documentation. The advanced connector policy API call is valid, but its note should identify the request-body properties that configure the allowlist and permitted actions.

claims.claim: Power Platform connectors wrap APIs to connect Power Apps, Power Automate and Copilot Studio to other services.
claims.quote: Connectors from Microsoft Power Platform act as proxies or "wrappers" around APIs. They enable Copilot Studio, Power Automate, Power Apps, and Azure Logic Apps to communicate with other apps and services.

claims.claim: Administrators use data policies to determine which connectors are usable and which can be combined.
claims.quote: Connectors can reside in only one data group at a time. By moving the Salesforce and SharePoint connectors to the Business data group, you're preventing users from creating flows and apps that combine these two connectors with any of the connectors in the Non-business or Blocked groups.

claims.claim: Connectors let apps read and write service data.
claims.quote: Power Apps retrieves table data into your app and updates data in your data source automatically.

claims.claim: SharePoint, SQL Server and Salesforce are examples of services reached through connectors.
claims.quote: Power Apps has connectors for many popular services and on-premises data sources, including SharePoint, SQL Server, Office 365, Salesforce, and Twitter.

claims.claim: A connection stores authentication credentials for a connector.
claims.quote: Connections are stored authentication credentials for a connector, such as OAuth credentials for the SharePoint connector.

claims.claim: Connections enable calls to connector operations, including actions and triggers.
claims.quote: You need to create a connection to your API in order to use that connection to call any operations that you expose in your custom connector.

claims.claim: A connector can provide tables, actions or both.
claims.quote: A connector might provide tables of data or actions. Some connectors provide only tables, some provide only actions, and some provide both.

claims.claim: For Power Apps and Power Automate use rights included with Microsoft 365, premium connectors require a standalone Power Apps or Power Automate plan.
claims.quote: A standalone Power Apps or Power Automate plan license is required to access all Premium, on-premises, and custom connectors.

claims.claim: A custom connector is a wrapper around a REST API defined by a maker or developer.
claims.quote: A custom connector is a wrapper around a REST API that lets Logic Apps, Power Automate flows, Power Apps, Copilot Studio agents and workflows, or Microsoft Copilot plugins communicate with that REST or SOAP API.

claims.claim: The SQL Server connector offers Microsoft Entra Integrated authentication.
claims.quote: For instance, the SQL Server connector allows you to use Microsoft Entra Integrated, SQL Server Authentication, and Windows Authentication.

claims.claim: The SQL Server connector offers SQL Server Authentication.

claims.claim: A shared connection uses the author's authentication implicitly for end users, with newer connections secured as described in Risks and limits.
claims.quote: In a shared connection, the Power Apps author provides the user name and password for the connection when creating the data source in the application. The connection authentication to the data source is then implicitly shared with end users.

claims.where: A different use of the word
claims.claim: Microsoft 365 Copilot connectors were formerly called Microsoft Graph connectors.
claims.quote: You can use Microsoft 365 Copilot connectors (formerly Microsoft Graph connectors) to bring data from external services into Microsoft Graph.

claims.where: A different use of the word
claims.claim: Synced Copilot connectors crawl and index external content into Microsoft Graph, unlike operational Power Platform connectors.
claims.quote: Synced connectors crawl and index content from external sources into Microsoft Graph.

claims.where: A different use of the word
claims.claim: Federated Copilot connectors fetch data in real time without indexing it into Microsoft 365.
claims.quote: Federated connectors use an MCP model to fetch data in real time, without indexing content into Microsoft 365.

claims.claim: Data policies classify connectors into Business, Non-Business and Blocked groups.
claims.quote: The three data groups are the Business data group, the Non-Business data group, and the Blocked data group.

claims.claim: Connectors in different data groups cannot be combined in one app or flow.
claims.quote: Makers can't create an app or flow that uses both the SharePoint and Gmail connectors.

claims.claim: A connector classified Blocked cannot be used where the policy applies.
claims.quote: Blocked connectors can't be used where this policy is applied.

claims.claim: A data policy protects the environments in its scope.
claims.quote: Tenant-level policies can be defined to include or exclude specific environments.

claims.claim: Microsoft's example allows any connector combination in environments to which no data policy applies.
claims.quote: Because no data policy is applied to test environments, apps and flows can use any set of connectors together in these environments.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risks and limits: New connectors; What to check
claims.claim: A new data policy initially places all connectors in Non-Business.
claims.quote: When you create a new policy, all connectors are placed in the Non-Business group by default.

claims.claim: For Power Apps and Power Automate use rights included with Microsoft 365, on-premises connectors require a standalone Power Apps or Power Automate plan.
claims.quote: A standalone Power Apps or Power Automate plan license is required to access all Premium, on-premises, and custom connectors.

claims.claim: Copilot Studio premium connectors are available in select Copilot Studio plans.
claims.quote: Premium connectors, which are available in select Copilot Studio plans.

claims.claim: An app using at least one premium connector is designated Premium.
claims.quote: An app that uses at least one premium connector, a custom connector, or an on-premises gateway.

claims.claim: An app using a custom connector is designated Premium.
claims.quote: An app that uses at least one premium connector, a custom connector, or an on-premises gateway.

claims.claim: An app using an on-premises gateway is designated Premium.
claims.quote: An app that uses at least one premium connector, a custom connector, or an on-premises gateway.

claims.claim: Microsoft reclassified several connectors from Standard to Premium in 2019.
claims.quote: Starting October 2019, several connectors are reclassified from Standard to Premium.

claims.claim: The reclassified connectors include SQL Server, Azure SQL and Dynamics 365.
claims.quote:
Premium connectors list:

claims.claim: The Power Platform licensing FAQ says extended use rights concluded on October 1, 2024.
claims.quote: The period for extended use rights concludes on October 1, 2024 and users are required to have appropriate licenses to maintain compliance.

claims.claim: The Power Platform licensing FAQ gives April 1, 2025 for in-product licensing enforcement.
claims.quote: In-product licensing enforcement begins April 1, 2025, until which your users are able to use these apps and flows.

claims.claim: The Power Apps licensing FAQ refers to licensing enforcement beginning February 2027.
claims.quote: This article lists common questions and answers to help you determine which Power Apps licenses your makers and users need, resolve trial and access issues, and prepare for licensing enforcement beginning February 2027.

claims.claim: Microsoft directs readers to the Power Apps pricing guide.
claims.quote: Take a look at the Power Apps pricing guide for details.

claims.claim: New connectors added after policy creation go into the designated default group.
claims.quote: You must designate one data group as the default group to automatically classify any new connectors added to Microsoft Power Platform after you create your policy.

claims.claim: Microsoft recommends retaining Non-Business as the default group for new connectors.
claims.quote: We recommend keeping the default setting as Non-business to map any new connectors added to Power Platform by default.

claims.claim: When the default group is Blocked, newly added unblockable connectors are assigned Non-Business instead.
claims.quote: However, any new connectors that are unblockable are mapped to Non-business because by design they can't be blocked.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Some connectors cannot be blocked
claims.claim: Classic data policies cannot block core connectors such as Dataverse, Approvals and Notifications.
claims.quote: To ensure core user scenarios remain fully functional, you can't block connectors that drive core Microsoft Power Platform functionality, such as Dataverse, Approvals, and Notifications.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Some connectors cannot be blocked
claims.claim: SharePoint is among the connectors that classic data policies cannot block.
claims.quote: For connectors like SharePoint that aren't blockable, the Block action isn't available and a warning appears.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Some connectors cannot be blocked
claims.claim: Nonblockable connectors can be classified Business or Non-Business.
claims.quote: You can classify these nonblockable connectors into Business or Non-Business data groups.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Some connectors cannot be blocked
claims.claim: Advanced connector policies can block otherwise nonblockable connectors on managed environments.
claims.quote: On managed environments (single or environment group), you can block any connector or any action, including those that are nonblockable in classic data policies.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Some connectors cannot be blocked
claims.claim: Nonblockable connectors remain nonblockable on non-managed environments.
claims.quote: However, on non-managed environments, the nonblockable connectors remain nonblockable.

claims.claim: Child flows share an internal dependency with the HTTP connector.
claims.quote: Because child flows share an internal dependency with the HTTP connector, the grouping that admins choose for HTTP connectors in a data policy might affect the ability to run child flows in that environment or tenant.

claims.where: Risks and limits: HTTP classification; What to check
claims.claim: The HTTP connector's classification can affect whether child flows run in an environment or tenant.
claims.quote: The grouping that admins choose for HTTP connectors in a data policy might affect the ability to run child flows in that environment or tenant.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Custom connectors; controls[1]; What to check
claims.claim: Tenant-level data policies classify custom connectors by host URL patterns.
claims.quote: Tenant admins can use the Power Platform admin center and PowerShell to classify custom connector by their Host URL endpoints using a pattern matching construct for tenant-level data policies.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Custom connectors; What to check
claims.claim: The wildcard custom connector pattern defaults to Ignore in new data policies.
claims.quote: By default, the pattern is set as Ignore for new data policies.

claims.claim: Ignore defers custom connector classification to other environment-level or tenant-level policies.
claims.quote: Ignore ignores data policies classification for all connectors in this tenant-level policy, and defers evaluation of a pattern to other environments or tenant-level policies

claims.claim: Custom connector data policy evaluation happens before Set Host URL.
claims.quote: Custom connector evaluation with data policies happens before the use of Set Host URL

claims.claim: Set Host URL can dynamically point a custom connector to another REST API.
claims.quote: Set Host URL which can dynamically change the custom connector to point to any other REST API.

claims.claim: Custom connector data policy enforcement does not apply to apps last published before October 2020.
claims.quote: The use of custom connectors isn't enforced by data policies in apps that were last published before October 2020.

claims.claim: Some apps published before October 1, 2020 require republishing for connector action rules to be enforced.
claims.quote: Some Power Apps, published before October 1, 2020, need to be republished for connector action rules to enforce data policies.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Advanced connector policies
claims.claim: ACP enforcement begins on saving a single-environment policy or publishing an environment-group policy.
claims.quote: ACP enforces a strict allowlist as soon as you save it (single environment) or publish it (environment group): every connector that isn't explicitly allowed is blocked.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Advanced connector policies
claims.claim: ACP blocks every connector that is not explicitly allowed.
claims.quote: ACP enforces a strict allowlist as soon as you save it (single environment) or publish it (environment group): every connector that isn't explicitly allowed is blocked.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Advanced connector policies; Open questions
claims.claim: ACP design-time enforcement is rolling out separately across maker portals.
claims.quote:
Design-time enforcement is rolling out across maker portals in the following order:
1. Power Automate maker portal — rolling out first
2. Copilot Studio — following Power Automate
3. Power Apps maker portal — following Copilot Studio

claims.where: Risks and limits: Advanced connector policies; Open questions
claims.claim: ACP is runtime-only for a workload until that maker portal receives design-time enforcement, which marks its general availability.
claims.quote: Each maker portal's release of design-time enforcement for ACP marks the general availability of ACP for that workload. Until design-time support is available in a given maker portal, ACP operates as a runtime-only enforcement for that workload.

claims.claim: All newly created shared connections after January 2024 are secured.
claims.quote: However, after January 2024, all newly created shared connections are secured.

claims.claim: Apps using earlier shared connections need republishing to secure them.
claims.quote: To secure existing apps, republish them.

claims.claim: Microsoft advises a maximum of 10 connectors per canvas app.
claims.quote: Keep the number of connectors in a canvas app to a maximum of 10, and connection references to no more than 20.

claims.claim: Microsoft advises no more than 20 connection references per canvas app.
claims.quote: Keep the number of connectors in a canvas app to a maximum of 10, and connection references to no more than 20.

claims.claim: Exceeding the recommended connector and connection-reference counts can lengthen app loading and cause saving problems.
claims.quote: Going beyond these limits can lead to longer loading times for users when launching the app and can cause problems when saving the app.

claims.claim: The prebuilt classification control is at Power Platform admin center > Security > Settings > Data and privacy > Data policy > policy > Edit Policy > Prebuilt connectors > connector > Move to Business.
claims.quote: Select one or more pre-built connectors. For this walkthrough, select the Salesforce and SharePoint connectors, and then select Move to Business from the top menu bar.

claims.claim: Add-ConnectorsToPolicy -PolicyName <policy GUID> -Classification <General|Confidential|Blocked> -Connectors <connector objects> sets a connector's classification.
claims.quote: The Add-ConnectorsToPolicy takes the connectors as a list of objects and adds them to the specified group of the given DLP policy. If any of the connectors are already classified in a different group, they are moved to the specified group.

claims.claim: The tenant-level data policy instructions require the Power Platform Administrator role.
claims.quote: To follow the steps described in this article for tenant-level policies, sign in as a user with the Power Platform Administrator role.

claims.claim: Environment-level policy instructions require Environment Admin permissions, subject to the Dataverse qualification stated in the prose.
claims.quote: To follow the steps for environment-level policies, you need to have Power Apps Environment Admin permissions. For environments with a Dataverse database, you need to be assigned the System Administrator role instead.

claims.claim: General, Confidential and Blocked map respectively to Non-business, Business and Blocked.
claims.quote: Allowed values are 'General', 'Confidential', and 'Blocked' (for Non-business, Business, and Blocked, respectively).

claims.claim: The custom URL-pattern control is at Power Platform admin center > Security > Settings > Data and privacy > Data policy > policy > Edit Policy > Custom connectors > Add connector pattern.
claims.quote: You can add new rules by selecting Add connector pattern on the Custom connectors page.

claims.claim: New-PowerAppPolicyUrlPatterns -TenantId <tenant ID> -PolicyName <policy GUID> -NewUrlPatterns <URL patterns object> creates custom connector URL-pattern rules.
claims.quote:
New-PowerAppPolicyUrlPatterns
    -TenantId <String>
    -PolicyName <String>
    -NewUrlPatterns <Object>

claims.claim: The URL-pattern cmdlet reference limits the operation to tenant-level policies.
claims.quote: Currently, this cmdlet is only enabled for polices at the tenant level.

claims.claim: Environment-level data policies classify individual custom connectors by name.
claims.quote: Environment admins can use the Power Platform admin center to classify individual, custom connectors by name for environment-level data policies.

claims.claim: Connector action control is at Power Platform admin center > Security > Data and privacy > Data policy > policy > Edit policy > Prebuilt connectors > connector > More actions > Configure connectors > Connector actions.
claims.quote:
In the Prebuilt connectors section, select a Blockable connector and then select More actions next to it.
6. Select Configure connectors and then Connector actions.

claims.claim: New-PowerAppDlpPolicyConnectorConfigurations -TenantId <tenant ID> -PolicyName <policy GUID> -NewDlpPolicyConnectorConfigurations <connector configurations> sets connector action rules.
claims.quote: New-PowerAppDlpPolicyConnectorConfigurations -TenantId $TenantId -PolicyName $PolicyName -NewDlpPolicyConnectorConfigurations $ConnectorConfigurations

claims.claim: Classic connector action control supports blockable connectors, not unblockable connectors.
claims.quote: You can configure connector actions for all blockable connectors, but not for unblockable connectors and custom connectors.

claims.claim: Classic connector action control does not support custom connectors.
claims.quote: You can configure connector actions for all blockable connectors, but not for unblockable connectors and custom connectors.

claims.claim: Allowing and blocking individual triggers in classic connector action control is currently PowerShell-only.
claims.quote: Support for allowing and blocking individual triggers is currently available only via PowerShell.

claims.claim: Administrators need maker access to Power Apps to retrieve the connector action list.
claims.quote: The admin must sign in to Power Apps and have access to complete the user consent process. If the admin doesn't have access to Power Apps, then the list of connector actions won't be retrieved.

claims.claim: Environment-group ACP configuration is at Power Platform admin center > Manage > Environment groups > environment group > Rules > Advanced connector policies.
claims.quote:
The environment group's page is displayed. Select the Rules tab.
6. Select Advanced connector policies. The Advanced connector policies pane is displayed.

claims.claim: POST https://api.powerplatform.com/governance/ruleBasedPolicies?api-version=2024-10-01 creates an advanced connector policy with its allowlist and action settings.
claims.quote: An advanced connector policy is a rule-based policy that contains a rule set with the ID ConnectorManagement. That rule set carries a version and its inputs hold an AllowedConnectorList
claims.fix: Keep the call unchanged. Add to controls[3].note and the rendered note: 'The request body sets ruleSets[].inputs.AllowedConnectorList in the ConnectorManagement rule set; entries use AllowedConnector, AllowedActionsMode and AllowedActions to select connectors and actions.'

claims.claim: Environment-group ACP rules must be published after saving.
claims.quote:
When all connectors are set as you require, select Save.
9. The environment group's page is redisplayed. After you update all rules to your requirements, select Publish rules in the command bar.

claims.claim: The single-environment ACP route is Power Platform admin center > Security > Data and privacy > Advanced connector policies.
claims.quote:
In the navigation pane, select Security.
3. In the Security pane, select Data and privacy.
4. Select Advanced connector policies.

claims.claim: Assigning a newly created ACP policy to an environment group requires a second POST.
claims.quote: Adding ACP to an environment group is a two-part operation: create the policy, then assign it to the group. The create call returns the new policy id, which you use in the assignment call.

claims.claim: Creating, editing or deleting data policies requires Environment Admin or Power Platform admin permissions, with the stated Dataverse qualification.
claims.quote: To create, edit, or delete data policies, you must have either Environment Admin or Power Platform admin permissions.

claims.claim: Environment-level data policies for environments with a Dataverse database require the System Administrator role instead.
claims.quote: For environments with a Dataverse database, you need to be assigned the System Administrator role instead.

claims.claim: Environment admins cannot edit policies created by tenant admins.
claims.quote: Environment admins can't edit policies created by the tenant admin.

claims.claim: Environment admins cannot delete policies created by tenant admins.
claims.quote: Environment admins can't delete policies created by the tenant admin.

claims.claim: Environment-level data policies cannot override tenant-wide data policies.
claims.quote: Environment-level data policies can't override tenant-wide data policies.

claims.claim: ACP initially uses mixed mode.
claims.quote: Mixed mode is the default state when you first enable ACP: classic data policies continue to be evaluated alongside your new advanced connector policy until you switch to ACP-only mode.

claims.claim: Mixed mode applies the most restrictive settings from ACP and classic data policies together.
claims.quote: ACP runs alongside classic data policies, and the most restrictive settings from both are enforced.

claims.claim: ACP-only mode ignores classic data policies for the affected scope.
claims.quote: All classic data policies are ignored for those environments, even if they're still configured.

claims.claim: ACP-only mode does not delete classic data policy configurations.
claims.quote: Data policy configurations aren't deleted. They remain in place but aren't enforced while ACP-only mode is active.

claims.claim: Classic data policies continue to provide action control and endpoint filtering alongside ACP.
claims.quote: This approach allows you to complement configurations so that data policies can achieve action control and endpoint filtering until such time as those features are native to ACP.

claims.claim: Get-AdminPowerAppConnection returns connections from environments where the caller is an environment admin.
claims.quote: Returns all connections from all environments where the calling user is an environment admin. For global admins, this searches across all environments in the tenant.

claims.claim: Get-AdminPowerAppConnector lists custom connectors in the tenant.
claims.quote:
Get-AdminPowerAppConnector
```

Returns a list of all custom connector details in the tenant.

claims.claim: Get-AdminPowerAppConnector does not list custom connectors in a solution.
claims.quote: Get-AdminPowerAppConnector doesn't list custom connectors that are in a solution. This is a known limitation.

claims.claim: Enforcing data policies on connections disables existing connections that violate those policies.
claims.quote: Enforcing disables existing connections that violate data policies and enables any previously disabled connections that no longer violate data policies.

claims.claim: Microsoft says custom connector support for ACP is planned.
claims.quote: Custom connectors | Not yet supported | Planned as a separate rule type in a future release.

claims.claim: Microsoft says HTTP connector support for ACP is planned.
claims.quote: HTTP connectors | Not yet supported | Planned alongside custom connector support.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans Power Platform admin center support for allowing and blocking individual triggers.
claims.quote: Support is planned for the Power Platform admin center in the future.
